sources.entry: Overkill - Stop iTunes from opening when you connect your iPhone.
Overkill - Stop iTunes from opening when you connect your iPhone.

summary.one_liner: Overkill is a small background Mac app that automatically quits iTunes (and optionally other apps) whenever it launches, such as when an iPhone is connected.
summary.what_it_does: Overkill runs silently in the background on macOS and kills iTunes so it does not interrupt work when it opens, for example when an iPhone is plugged in. A menu bar control lets the user pause Overkill temporarily, for instance to use iTunes for a movie night. Users can add other Mac apps to the kill list, such as the Photos app. The README describes it as having no CPU usage from polling and no analytics, and as roughly 300 lines of native Mac code. It supports Dark and Light menu bar modes and auto start at login. It can be installed by downloading the app or through Homebrew.
use_cases: stop iTunes opening when iPhone is connected
block automatic app launches on Mac
background utility to close unwanted apps
how_to_run: Download Overkill from the link in the README and open the Overkill icon
Or install with Homebrew: brew cask install overkill
stack: Objective-C or Swift (not named in README)
notable: Kills iTunes automatically whenever it launches, including on iPhone connection
Menu bar pause option for times you want iTunes
Custom kill list supports any Mac app, not only iTunes
Lightweight design: no polling, no analytics, about 300 lines of code
caveats: Only runs on Mac; iTunes-focused and the README does not say whether it works on newer macOS versions
Credits earlier projects (noTunes, Overkill-OSX), suggesting it builds on prior work
Installation via Homebrew uses the older 'brew cask install' syntax shown in the README
